script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Last Shot

INT. CANTON GYM - DAY

A LARGE, RUSTIC GYM located in the heart of a small, rural town. The smell of sweat and rubber permeates the air. COACH JIMMY STARK, a burly, fifty-something man, stands in the center of the room, barking out instructions to his team of young basketball players.

COACH JIMMY
(yelling)
Alright, team! Defensive stance! Ready, set... GO!

As the kids scramble to take position, JIMMY's phone rings. He answers it with a sigh.

JIMMY
(into phone)
Yes, Coach Thompson? What's the news? All right, I'll be there tomorrow.

The coach hangs up the phone and turns to his team.

COACH JIMMY
(looking serious)
Pack your bags, team. We're heading to the city for a tournament tomorrow. Last chance to make a name for ourselves before the season ends.

EXT. TOWN SQUARE - DAY

The team, made up of ten kids ranging from ten to fifteen years old, gathers around their bus as their parents take photos and offer words of encouragement.

MRS. JENKINS, the team mother, hands EMMA, the team captain, a small, worn leather basketball.

MRS. JENKINS
(teary-eyed)
Emma, remember what your father always told you. Shoot for the stars.

Emma nods, clutching the ball tightly. Her father, who passed away last year, was the reason she fell in love with basketball in the first place.

INT. BUS - DAY

The team settles into their seats for the long ride to the city. EMMA sits in the front row, her eyes fixed on the basketball.

EMMA
(under her breath)
I've got this, Dad.

INT. CITY GYM - NIGHT

The team arrives at the gym where the tournament is being held. They're met with awe as they step off the bus, taking in the grandeur of the facility. They're assigned to their locker room, where they gather their gear and prepare for their first game the following morning.

EXT. CITY PARK - NIGHT

EMMA and a few teammates explore the city, marveling at the lights and sounds. They come across a basketball court and decide to shoot some hoops. EMMA takes a shot from the corner, but misses.

Suddenly, a figure emerges from the shadows. It's TYRONE, a local prodigy and the star player for the city's elite basketball team. He's impressed by EMMA's determination and offers her some advice.

TYRONE
You've got a strong shot, Emma. But you need to focus on your form. Your follow-through is off.

He demonstrates the correct form, and EMMA takes another shot. This time, it swishes through the net.

TYRONE
(smiling)
Now that's what I call a last shot.

INT. GYM - MORNING

The team's first game begins. They're matched against a formidable opponent, but EMMA's newfound focus pays off. She hits shot after shot, leading her team to a surprising victory.

INT. LOCKER ROOM - POST-GAME

The team celebrates their win, but EMMA is still reflecting on Tyrone's words. She decides to practice her form before their next game.

EXT. CITY GYM - NIGHT

EMMA spends hours in the gym, perfecting her shot. Her teammates join her, inspired by her dedication.

EXT. CITY STREETS - NIGHT

The team's second game is a tight one, but EMMA's improved shooting helps them pull out a win. They continue to make their way through the tournament, each game more challenging than the last.

INT. FINAL GAME - DAY

The team reaches the finals, facing off against the city's elite team. EMMA's confidence is high, but the pressure is mounting.

INT. GYM - FINAL QUARTER

EMMA's team is down by two points with only seconds remaining. She takes a deep breath and steps up to the line, her heart pounding in her chest.

EMMA
(to herself)
This is it, Dad.

She takes aim and releases the ball. The gym falls silent as it soars through the air. The ball hits nothing but net, and the crowd erupts into cheers.

EXT. GYM - POST-GAME

The team celebrates their victory, their small-town team name now etched in the city's history books. EMMA looks up at the banner, her father's words echoing in her mind.

EMMA
(whispering)
I shot for the stars, Dad. And I made it.

FADE OUT.
